title: Chapter 6 — Personal Brand and Communication
intro: How you present, speak, write, and follow up is the layer that carries every sale. People buy from people they trust — and trust starts with how you show up.

sections.title: You Are the Product
sections.content:
Before a customer evaluates the refrigerator, they evaluate you. Your appearance, your energy, your confidence, your professionalism — all of it forms an impression in the first thirty seconds.

This is not about wearing expensive clothes. It is about looking like someone who takes their job seriously. Clean, professional, put together. If you look like you care about yourself, customers assume you will care about their purchase.

The same applies to how you speak. Clear, confident, knowledgeable — but never arrogant. Customers want an expert they can trust, not a know-it-all they have to tolerate.

sections.title: Written Communication Matters
sections.content:
Every email, every text, every quote you send represents you. Typos, sloppy formatting, and unclear information tell the customer you are careless — even if you are not.

Keep written communication professional, clear, and concise. Reread before you send. Use the customer's name. Confirm details. Make it easy for them to say yes.

In a world where a lot of the buying process happens through screens, your written communication may be the only impression some customers ever have of you. Make it count.

sections.title: Follow-Up Is Communication
sections.content:
How you follow up communicates as much as what you say on the floor.

Fast follow-up says: I value your time and I am organized.
Slow follow-up says: you were not important enough to remember.
No follow-up says: I already got what I needed from you.

Every follow-up is a communication opportunity. It reinforces trust, keeps you top of mind, and moves the sale forward. The timing, the tone, and the content all matter.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating personal brand and communication, ask:

Does the salesperson present themselves professionally?
Is their written communication clear, accurate, and error-free?
Do they follow up promptly and consistently?
Do they communicate in a way that builds trust — or erodes it?

People remember how you made them feel long after they forget what you said about the product.
